beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: Dave lays three cards down, the shop nearly empty behind him. "One more, before we hand back the keys."

beats.prompt: The past: the quiet that let you finally see what wasn't working.
The present: the honest account that set things right between you two.
The future: the ending that's actually clearing room for the next place.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Quiz me on this one. If Death's not really about endings sealing shut, why does it still feel exactly like losing something?"

options.text: Because real change is intense and uncomfortable even when nothing's actually being erased.
It feels like loss because you are, in fact, losing it.
If it feels like loss, you're reading the card wrong.

elaboration: The card doesn't ask the discomfort to go away — real transformation is intense and a little uncomfortable, and that's still true even though nothing here is being sealed shut.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "How do I know what's actually worth carrying to the new place, and what's just dead weight I'm dragging along out of guilt?"

options.text: Look underneath the sentiment for what's actually still alive and useful — the rest can go.
It doesn't matter what you bring, the card doesn't care.

elaboration: Death asks you to look beneath the surface for what's actually still got life in it — the rest was already dead weight, guilt or no guilt.

beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: "One thread ties all three: the quiet that showed you the problem, the honest fix that followed, and the ending that's making room for the next chapter."

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Yeah. I think I've been treating the garage like something that needed protecting, instead of something that already did its job. Feels right to let it go now. Thanks — for all of it, really."
